<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

Everything is built in the daemon's community module and its HTTP and CLI verbs, on the machinery role templates already use: versioned shipped originals compiled into the daemon, a governance copy a repo owns, and the single writer that commits every governance change with its reason. PRD 006 adds the type catalog and seeds, the type on the role document and the holding, and the retype migration. PRD 007 builds on it: launch settings, the assembled first turn, spawn with a role and close with --stop. PRD 008 defines pods as governance folders driven by the same spawn and close paths, once per member. PRD 010 ships pod templates and the adopt, diff, init and export verbs. Nothing adds a loop, poll or timer, no permission rule changes, and no existing JSON field is removed. This PR (PRD 006) carries the components PRD 006 builds. The rest of the design, designed with them in workstream 006 s01, lands with its PRD so that every component is built by a step the moment it appears: PRD 007 adds launch settings and parameters on a role, the assembled first turn, spawn with a role, seats with no role in the view, suggest and close with --stop; PRD 008 the pod definition and the pod verbs; PRD 010 the shipped pod templates with adopt, diff, init and export; and the concepts page is PRD 009's.

<a id="decisions"></a>

## Decisions

| id | decision | why | realises |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| d-1 | The type is recorded on the role, and a seat's type is derived from the roles it holds; authority still comes from today's seat role (`prime` designation, `pm`, `pa`, `worker`) and is not recomputed from the type. | Ruling of 2026-11-25: one label per seat and no permission change (PRD 003 out of scope). Deriving authority from the type would let a role typed project-manager grant pm powers to a seat that has none today. `type` is added to every JSON output; no existing field is removed or renamed, since the extensions, the statusline and other projects read them. A redundant field is proposed for later cleanup, not dropped. | [req-05](../prds/006-seat-types.dd.md#requirements) |
| d-2 | Types are pij's fixed set in a versioned catalog shipped with the daemon; a repo copies and edits seeds, not types. | A repo cannot add a type (non-goal n-4). Shipping definitions as immutable versions mirrors role templates, so PRD 010 can copy and diff them with the same machinery. | [req-02](../prds/006-seat-types.dd.md#requirements), [req-06](../prds/006-seat-types.dd.md#requirements), [req-08](../prds/006-seat-types.dd.md#requirements) |
| d-3 | A fixed rule is checked when a role document is written (add, edit, retype), not enforced on a running seat. | Daemon enforcement of a type's rules is out of scope (n-1). Refusing a role document that removes a fixed rule is validation of the record, the same kind of check ddocs does. | [req-06](../prds/006-seat-types.dd.md#requirements) |
| d-4 | A role document's type is cached on its pointer row (`community_pointers.role_type`), so `pij list` reads no governance file. | `/v1/seats` serves every project and has no governance worktree to read; a file read per role per list would grow with seats. The pointer is already written after every directory commit and rebuilt from the branch head, so those are the cache's refresh points; only a hand edit of the branch can leave it stale, until the next rebuild. One row per role, so an assign writes nothing new. | [req-05](../prds/006-seat-types.dd.md#requirements) |
| d-5 | `kind` and `lifecycle` are retired, not deleted: optional in the schema, never written again, still read. | Role documents in five projects carry them; req-07 needs those to keep reading. retype proposes a type from the template first, then the id. | [req-07](../prds/006-seat-types.dd.md#requirements) |
| d-6 | One blueprint serves PRDs 006, 007, 008 and 010; each PRD's components join it in the PR that brings that PRD to main. | The PRDs land one PR at a time. ddocs refuses a link to a document not on the branch yet, and the coverage check refuses a component no workstream step builds, so a component appears with its PRD and the step that builds it. |  |
| d-7 | Role templates name their type through a table in the type catalog, not through new template versions. | A new version of every template would mark every existing role made from one as behind its template, and its diff would show only the type line. The table is read by add and retype alike; a template's next real version may carry `meta.type` itself, which then wins. | [req-01](../prds/006-seat-types.dd.md#requirements), [req-07](../prds/006-seat-types.dd.md#requirements) |
| d-8 | A spawn with a role makes one writer commit, holding the first-turn record and the holding, after the seat's row is written and before the bind wait or any delivery. | The daemon writes a seat's row only after tmux launches it, and a holding needs the row, so nothing can be committed before launch. Committing both together keeps the cost at a plain spawn plus one `pij directory assign` (PM ruling), and the seat still receives nothing until the commit has landed. A refused commit is a policy, not a brake: it decides that the spawn does not survive, and rolls it back through the one failed-row-write path. | [req-02](../prds/007-role-start.dd.md#requirements), [req-03](../prds/007-role-start.dd.md#requirements), [req-09](../prds/007-role-start.dd.md#requirements) |
| d-9 | `pij close --stop` stops the process pij recorded at launch, by pid and only while its start time still matches, after a ready answer: the memory turn ended within its bound and the seat wrote a memory note after the turn was delivered. | Every seat runs as one user, so stopping by name or pattern would reach other seats' processes (AGENTS rule 6). The start-time match keeps a reused pid safe. Ready is read from facts the daemon already records (the turn's idle, the note's spine event), so it adds no poll. | [req-12](../prds/007-role-start.dd.md#requirements) |

<a id="costs"></a>

## Costs

| id | what | rate | scaling | component |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| k-1 | `pij directory add/edit/types/retype` and seed edits. | on demand only: in-process file reads and the single writer's governance commit (the same git and ddocs launches an add makes today); `types` launches nothing | with the commands a seat runs; none per seat or per tick | [c-directory-type](#components), [c-retype](#components), [c-seeds](#components) |
| k-2 | A seat's type in `pij list` and `pij directory`. | 0 launches: one indexed store query per `/v1/seats` call (open holdings joined to pointers), so it also rides the calls that poll the roster (federation fan-in, about once a second per peer, and the extension roster); never per seat. Each directory write reads the role documents it committed once, in-process | with the rows listed; no loop, poll or timer | [c-seat-type](#components), [c-mixed-types](#components) |
| k-3 | Spawning with a role named, and closing with --stop. | a spawn with a role: the plain spawn's harness and tmux launches plus one writer commit (the launches of one `pij directory assign`); `--first-turn` 0 launches; close --stop: the existing memory turn plus one process start-time read and one signal | per spawn or close a seat asks for; nothing per tick per seat; no loop, poll or timer | [c-spawn-role](#components), [c-first-turn](#components), [c-close-stop](#components) |
| k-5 | Suggestions, creator notes and the no-role action. | suggest and its answer: one writer commit each; one FYI per role or seat created by a seat that is not the prime; the no-role action reads live seats the view already reads, with in-process path checks | on demand; the view's checks grow with live seats, per view only | [c-suggest](#components), [c-unregistered](#components) |
